cards.text: Moses is still speaking to all Israel, retelling their long trip through the wilderness. God has walked them right past Esau's descendants, Moab and Ammon, and told them to leave those lands alone (Deuteronomy 2:4-19). Now the LORD tells Moses, "Arise, set out, and cross the Arnon Valley."

cards.question: On the other side of the Arnon, the LORD says He has delivered a king and his land into Israel's hand. Which king?
Just like with Moab, the LORD tells Israel to leave Sihon's land alone.

cards.text: Then the LORD makes Moses a promise. Starting this very day, He will begin to put the dread and fear of Israel upon all the nations under heaven.

cards.question: When the nations under heaven hear the reports about Israel, how does the LORD say they will react?

answers.text: They will send gifts of peace
They will shrug off the news

cards.text: So Moses sends messengers from the Wilderness of Kedemoth to Sihon king of Heshbon. No group chat back then, friend. You want to reach a king, you send guys on FOOT and hope he doesn't leave you on read.

cards.question: What do Moses' messengers bring to Sihon king of Heshbon?

cards.text: Moses asks to pass through Sihon's land on the main road and promises, "We will not turn to the right or to the left." FRIEND, most people can't drive that straight with the GPS yelling at them.

cards.question: Moses offers to buy food and water from Sihon in exchange for ___.
Moses tells Sihon that Esau's descendants in Seir and the Moabites in Ar already let Israel do the same thing.

cards.text: Moses even says where they're headed: across the Jordan, into the land the LORD is giving them. Paying guests who stay on the road? Sihon, this is the easiest yes of your LIFE.

cards.question: How does Sihon king of Heshbon answer Moses' offer?

answers.text: He won't let them pass through
He lets them pass right through
He asks for twice the silver

cards.question: Moses tells Israel why Sihon wouldn't let them through. What does he say?

answers.text: The LORD made his heart obstinate
His people were begging for war
He had made a deal with Ammon

cards.text: Then the LORD tells Moses, "See, I have begun to deliver Sihon and his land over to you." And Sihon brings his whole army out for battle against Israel at Jahaz.

cards.question: At Jahaz, Israel defeats Sihon's army, but Sihon and his sons get away.

cards.text: Moses doesn't soften what comes next. Israel captures all of Sihon's cities and devotes the people of every city to destruction, including women and children, leaving no survivors.

cards.question: From the cities they captured, what does Israel carry off for themselves?

answers.text: Only the livestock and the plunder
Only the weapons and the chariots
Only the tents and the tools

cards.question: From Aroer on the rim of the Arnon Valley all the way to Gilead, not one city had ___ too high for Israel.

cards.text: Moses says the LORD our God gave them every one of those cities. But he also points out the places Israel didn't go, and I respect it, because when something's off limits on my cooling rack, the mustache STAYS HOME.

cards.question: While they're at it, Israel takes some of the land of the Ammonites.

cards.text: Israel turns up the road to Bashan, and here comes Og, king of Bashan, with his whole army to fight them at Edrei. One king down and another at the door, like clocking out and getting a "quick thing" text from the boss.

cards.question: Og and his whole army are coming at Edrei. What does the LORD tell Moses?

answers.text: Send him an offer of peace

cards.question: The LORD tells Moses to do to Og what he did to ___ king of the Amorites.

cards.text: So the LORD our God also delivers Og king of Bashan and his whole army into Israel's hands. They strike them down until no survivor is left.

cards.question: How many of Og's cities does Israel capture?

cards.text: That's the entire region of Argob, the kingdom of Og in Bashan. There isn't a single city they fail to take.

cards.question: Og's sixty cities in Bashan were easy targets, with no walls or gates.
What does Israel do with the people of Og's cities?

answers.text: The same as with Sihon's cities
Makes them pay a yearly tribute
Lets them move to another land

cards.text: The men, women and children of every city are destroyed. And just like before, Israel carries off the livestock and the plunder.

Moses sums up the land they took from the two kings of the Amorites across the Jordan: from the Arnon Valley to Mount Hermon, which the Sidonians call Sirion and the Amorites call Senir. That's all the cities of the plateau, all of Gilead and all of Bashan, as far as Salecah and Edrei.

cards.question: Moses drops in a side note: Og king of Bashan was the only one left of the remnant of the ___.
Moses says Og's bed is still in Rabbah of the Ammonites. What is it made of?

cards.text: Nine cubits long and four cubits wide. I spent YEARS in the back of a junk drawer, and nobody ever pointed at it and said, "That's where Papa used to sleep."
And that's where Moses leaves the two kings for now. Stick around, friend, because he is NOT done preaching yet.

findings.problem: The card says God has 'walked them right past' Ammon. In Deuteronomy 2:19 Israel is only approaching Ammon, and Deuteronomy 2:37 says 'you did not go near the land of the Ammonites.' Saying Israel passed Ammon stretches the text and runs against 2:37. Keep only that God told them to leave those lands alone.

rule.text: Retelling: Papa Dorin can retell in his own words and fill in what the text clearly implies. Scene-setting details are fine. He never says anything the text shows is wrong.

findings.problem: The answers don't sound alike. The right answer, 'They will tremble in anguish,' uses the text's wording. The wrong answer 'They will shrug off the news' is much more modern and casual than the other two, so it is easy to rule out.

rule.text: Don't let the right answer stand out. All the answers should sound alike. None should sound more like the Bible, or more modern, than the others.

findings.problem: The joke blends the modern comparison (group chats, being left on read) with the Bible setting (messengers sent on foot to a king) in one image. It should keep to one image.

rule.text: One image only. Never blend the comparison with the Bible setting.

findings.problem: Deuteronomy 2:30 gives the reason Sihon refused ('the LORD your God had made his spirit stubborn and his heart obstinate') and also the purpose: 'that He might deliver him into your hand.' No card tells or asks about the purpose. It is the key point of the verse and ties the refusal to the LORD's promise in 2:24.

rule.text: When the baker leaves Prep, they understand the whole passage without missing an important detail.

findings.problem: The wrong answer 'roofs' makes the line 'not one city had roofs too high for Israel,' which sounds silly. 'Hills' is weak too. A thoughtful baker can pick 'walls' without knowing the passage.

rule.text: All the answers are the same kind of thing, about the same length and the same tone. None are silly.

findings.problem: This setup card says Moses 'points out the places Israel didn't go.' The next card (card 20) asks whether Israel took Ammonite land. Together with card 1, which says God told them to leave Ammon alone, this setup rules out 'True' before the baker answers.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: The joke 'when something's off limits on my cooling rack, the mustache STAYS HOME' doesn't click right away. It isn't clear what is off limits, who made it off limits, or what 'the mustache stays home' means. A stranger would say 'huh?'

rule.text: It clicks instantly for any adult, with no explaining. If a stranger would say "huh?", rewrite it.

findings.problem: This summary card for the land boundaries (Deuteronomy 3:8-10) lists every item: the Arnon Valley, Mount Hermon, Sirion, Senir, the plateau, Gilead, Bashan, Salecah and Edrei. A long stretch should be summed up in a few words, with at most one standout detail.

rule.text: He says in a few words what it covers and doesn't go item by item. He can name a standout detail the text gives if it helps the stretch stick.

findings.problem: Deuteronomy 3:11 is set off in parentheses. The text leaves open who gives this note, but card 11 ('Moses drops in a side note') and card 12 ('Moses says Og's bed is still in Rabbah') both say it is Moses. The cards should tell the detail without naming who says it.

rule.text: Leave open what the text leaves open: who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.
